messages.author: f0c9fce6b5a83875
messages.subject: diary daily analysis with dyads
parts:
Hi 
I am using lavaan for analyzing my dyadic data (actor-partner interdependence model) and so far, for cross-sectional data analysis it has worked very well.
I always compare my "lavaan-results" with the results I get from SPSS, AMOS or Mplus, to be sure, that I am doing my analyses with lavaan right,

However, since I've been trying to analyse daily diary data in lavaan, I do not get the same results as before with cross-sectional data.

I used available data and codes from :   http://www.intensivelongitudinal.com/ch8/ch8index.html
In the attachment files you will find the Mplus, Spss ( I get this from the website) and my lavaan syntax and results.

NOTE: 
coupleid = couple number
personid = person number
time day = 0-20
time7c = centering, so that zero is the midway through the 10 th diary day
freldis = female disatisfaction
fwrkstrs = female stress
fwrkstrsc = female stress grand-mean centered across male and female, across all diary days
separation of variation: 
fwrkstrscb = female between person mean 
fwrkstrscw = female within person variation, deviation of each persons fwrkstrsc score at a particuar time point from their own person-mean score.
analogue for male 

I highlighted the effects that should be the same.

The between person effects (and also variances and covariances) are not the same.
Does anybody know, if it is possible to calculate these analysis (with between and within person effects) as in Spss and Mplus at all?

Thank you for your help!

Claudia

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: diary daily analysis with dyads
parts: However, since I've been trying to analyse daily diary data in lavaan, I do not get the same results as before with cross-sectional data. I used available data and codes from :   http://www.intensivelongitudinal.com/ch8/ch8index.html

The Mplus syntax is fitting a multilevel model, which is not (yet) a feature available in lavaan.  If you open the zipped file of R syntax on the same page, you will notice the example does not use lavaan, it uses the lme() function from the nlme package -- you should use that example.  Eventually (version 0.6 according to rumors, many moons from now), lavaan will be able to fit multilevel data, but using the GLLAMM approach.  So you probably still wouldn't be able to exactly reproduce the Mplus output, which uses a somewhat different generalized latent variable model.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

Thank you very much for your answer!!

For me it is very helpful to know, that it isn't possible yet to calculate a multilevel model in lavaan. So, I will not try to change the model anymore until it fits ;).
I am looking forward to this multilevel sem feature (when it will be available) in lavaan.

Claudia
